sanskrit: mukhataḥ so 'gnim asṛjat prāṇād vāyum athāpi ca sarasvatīṃ ca vedāṃś ca manasaḥ sasṛje 'cyutaḥ
english: From his mouth he brought forth Agni, and from his breath the Wind as well; and from his mind the Imperishable One created Sarasvatī and the Vedas.

sanskrit: eṣa lokān sasarjādau devāṃś carṣigaṇaiḥ saha nidhanaṃ caiva mṛtyuṃ ca prajānāṃ prabhavo 'vyayaḥ
english: He it was who in the beginning created the worlds, the gods together with the hosts of seers, and death and destruction too—the imperishable source of all creatures.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmaś ca dharmajño varadaḥ sarvakāmadaḥ eṣa kartā ca kāryaṃ ca pūrvadevaḥ svayaṃprabhuḥ
english: He is the Law and the knower of the Law, the granter of boons, the fulfiller of every desire; he is the doer and the deed, the primeval god, self-luminous.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca pūrvam etad akalpayat ubhe saṃdhye diśaḥ khaṃ ca niyamaṃ ca janārdanaḥ
english: What has been, what is, and what is yet to come—all this Janārdana ordained of old, and the two twilights, the directions, the sky, and the ruling order.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṃś caiva hi govindas tapaś caivānu kalpayat sraṣṭāraṃ jagataś cāpi mahātmā prabhur avyayaḥ
english: Govinda likewise fashioned the seers and austerity in their turn, and the great-souled, imperishable lord shaped the Creator of the world as well.

sanskrit: agrajaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ saṃkarṣaṇam akalpayat śeṣaṃ cākalpayad devam anantam iti yaṃ viduḥ
english: He fashioned Saṃkarṣaṇa, firstborn of all beings, and he fashioned too the divine Śeṣa, whom men know as the Endless One.

sanskrit: yo dhārayati bhūtāni dharāṃ cemāṃ saparvatām dhyānayogena viprāś ca taṃ vadanti mahaujasam
english: He who upholds all beings and this earth with its mountains—him the brāhmaṇas, through the yoga of meditation, declare to be of mighty splendor.

sanskrit: karṇasrotodbhavaṃ cāpi madhuṃ nāma mahāsuram tam ugram ugrakarmāṇam ugrāṃ buddhiṃ samāsthitam brahmaṇo 'pacitiṃ kurvañ jaghāna puruṣottamaḥ
english: And the great asura named Madhu, sprung from the channel of his ear—fierce, fierce in deeds, set upon a fierce design—him the Supreme Person slew, doing honor to Brahmā.

sanskrit: tasya tāta vadhād eva devadānavamānavāḥ madhusūdanam ity āhur ṛṣayaś ca janārdanam varāhaś caiva siṃhaś ca trivikramagatiḥ prabhuḥ
english: From that slaying, my son, gods, dānavas, and men, and the seers, call Janārdana the Slayer of Madhu; and the lord is also the Boar, the Lion, and he whose stride spans the three worlds.

sanskrit: eṣa mātā pitā caiva sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ hariḥ paraṃ hi puṇḍarīkākṣān na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
english: Hari is the mother and the father of all living things; for higher than the lotus-eyed one nothing has ever been, nor ever shall be.

sanskrit: mukhato 'sṛjad brāhmaṇān bāhubhyāṃ kṣatriyāṃs tathā vaiśyāṃś cāpy ūruto rājañ śūdrān padbhyāṃ tathaiva ca tapasā niyato devo nidhānaṃ sarvadehinām
english: From his mouth he brought forth the brāhmaṇas, from his arms the kṣatriyas, from his thighs, O king, the vaiśyas, and from his feet the śūdras—the god, bound to austerity, the resting-place of all embodied beings.

sanskrit: brahmabhūtam amāvāsyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tathaiva ca yogabhūtaṃ paricaran keśavaṃ mahad āpnuyāt
english: He who, at the new moon and the full moon alike, attends in worship upon Keśava, become one with brahman and become one with yoga, shall attain the great goal.

sanskrit: keśavaḥ paramaṃ tejaḥ sarvalokapitāmahaḥ evam āhur hṛṣīkeśaṃ munayo vai narādhipa
english: Keśava is the supreme radiance, the grandsire of all the worlds; thus, O lord of men, do the sages speak of Hṛṣīkeśa.

sanskrit: evam enaṃ vijānīhi ācāryaṃ pitaraṃ gurum kṛṣṇo yasya prasīdeta lokās tenākṣayā jitāḥ
english: Know him, then, to be teacher, father, and guru; he with whom Kṛṣṇa is pleased has thereby won the imperishable worlds.

sanskrit: yaś caivainaṃ bhayasthāne keśavaṃ śaraṇaṃ vrajet sadā naraḥ paṭhaṃś cedaṃ svastimān sa sukhī bhavet
english: And the man who in a place of fear takes refuge in this Keśava, and who ever recites this hymn, shall be safe and shall be happy.

sanskrit: ye ca kṛṣṇaṃ prapadyante te na muhyanti mānavāḥ bhaye mahati ye magnāḥ pāti nityaṃ janārdanaḥ
english: Those mortals who take refuge in Kṛṣṇa do not fall into bewilderment; those sunk in great peril Janārdana ever protects.

sanskrit: etad yudhiṣṭhiro jñātvā yāthātathyena bhārata sarvātmanā mahātmānaṃ keśavaṃ jagadīśvaram prapannaḥ śaraṇaṃ rājan yogānām īśvaraṃ prabhum
english: Knowing all this in its very truth, O Bhārata, Yudhiṣṭhira with his whole being took refuge in the great-souled Keśava, lord of the world, O king—the lord and master of all yogas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu cedaṃ mahārāja brahmabhūtastavaṃ mama brahmarṣibhiś ca devaiś ca yaḥ purā kathito bhuvi
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear now from me too, O great king, this Hymn to the One Become Brahman, which of old upon the earth was uttered by the brahmā-seers and by the gods.

sanskrit: sādhyānām api devānāṃ devadeveśvaraḥ prabhuḥ lokabhāvanabhāvajña iti tvāṃ nārado 'bravīt bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca mārkaṇḍeyo 'bhyuvāca ha
english: "Lord and god of the gods, even of the Sādhya gods, knower of the being and becoming of the worlds"—so Nārada addressed you; and Mārkaṇḍeya called you what has been, what is, and what shall be.

sanskrit: yajñānāṃ caiva yajñaṃ tvāṃ tapaś ca tapasām api devānām api devaṃ ca tvām āha bhagavān bhṛguḥ purāṇe bhairavaṃ rūpaṃ viṣṇo bhūtapateti vai
english: The sacrifice of sacrifices, the austerity of austerities, the god even of the gods—so the blessed Bhṛgu named you, O Viṣṇu, of awful form in days of yore, lord of all beings.

sanskrit: vāsudevo vasūnāṃ tvaṃ śakraṃ sthāpayitā tathā devadevo 'si devānām iti dvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: "You are Vāsudeva among the Vasus, and the establisher of Śakra; you are the god of the gods"—so Dvaipāyana declared.

sanskrit: pūrve prajānisargeṣu dakṣam āhuḥ prajāpatim sraṣṭāraṃ sarvabhūtānām aṅgirās tvāṃ tato 'bravīt
english: "In the first creations of creatures they call Dakṣa the Lord of Beings, the maker of all that lives"—so then Aṅgiras spoke of you.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ te śarīrotthaṃ vyaktaṃ te manasi sthitam devā vāksaṃbhavāś ceti devalas tv asito 'bravīt
english: "The unmanifest arises from your body, the manifest abides in your mind, and the gods are born of your speech"—so Asita Devala spoke.

sanskrit: śirasā te divaṃ vyāptaṃ bāhubhyāṃ pṛthivī dhṛtā jaṭharaṃ te trayo lokāḥ puruṣo 'si sanātanaḥ
english: By your head the heaven is filled, by your arms the earth is upheld; your belly is the three worlds—you are the eternal Person.

sanskrit: evaṃ tvām abhijānanti tapasā bhāvitā narāḥ ātmadarśanatṛptānām ṛṣīṇāṃ cāpi sattamaḥ
english: Thus do men matured by austerity come to know you; and you are the best even of those seers who are content in the vision of the Self.

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇām udārāṇām āhaveṣv anivartinām sarvadharmapradhānānāṃ tvaṃ gatir madhusūdana
english: Of the noble royal seers, who never turn back in battle, who hold all duty foremost—of these you are the goal, O Slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: eṣa te vistaras tāta saṃkṣepaś ca prakīrtitaḥ keśavasya yathātattvaṃ suprīto bhava keśave
english: This, my son, is the full account and the brief account alike, proclaimed of Keśava as it truly is; be well pleased with Keśava.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca puṇyaṃ śrutvaitad ākhyānaṃ mahārāja sutas tava keśavaṃ bahu mene sa pāṇḍavāṃś ca mahārathān
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard this holy tale, O great king, your son held Keśava in high regard, and the Pāṇḍavas too, those mighty warriors.

sanskrit: tam abravīn mahārāja bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ punaḥ māhātmyaṃ te śrutaṃ rājan keśavasya mahātmanaḥ
english: To him, O great king, Bhīṣma the son of Śāntanu spoke again: You have heard, O king, the greatness of the great-souled Keśava.

sanskrit: narasya ca yathātattvaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi yadarthaṃ nṛṣu saṃbhūtau naranārāyaṇāv ubhau
english: And you have heard the truth of Nara as well, of which you asked me—wherefore the two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, were born among men.

sanskrit: avadhyau ca yathā vīrau saṃyugeṣv aparājitau yathā ca pāṇḍavā rājann agamyā yudhi kasya cit
english: And how those two heroes are not to be slain, unconquered in their encounters, and how the Pāṇḍavas, O king, are not to be reached in battle by any man.

sanskrit: prītimān hi dṛḍhaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pāṇḍaveṣu yaśasviṣu tasmād bravīmi rājendra śamo bhavatu pāṇḍavaiḥ
english: For Kṛṣṇa is firmly devoted to the glorious Pāṇḍavas; therefore I say to you, O lord of kings: let there be peace with the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pṛthivīṃ bhuṅkṣva sahito bhrātṛbhir balibhir vaśī naranārāyaṇau devāv avajñāya naśiṣyasi
english: Self-mastered, enjoy the earth together with your strong brothers; but if you slight the divine Nara and Nārāyaṇa, you shall perish.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tava pitā tūṣṇīm āsīd viśāṃ pate vyasarjayac ca rājānaṃ śayanaṃ ca viveśa ha
english: Having spoken thus, your father fell silent, O lord of peoples, and dismissed the king and went in to his couch.

sanskrit: rājāpi śibiraṃ prāyāt praṇipatya mahātmane śiśye ca śayane śubhre tāṃ rātriṃ bharatarṣabha
english: The king too, having bowed to the great-souled one, went off to his camp and lay that night upon his bright couch, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyuṣitāyāṃ ca śarvaryām udite ca divākare ubhe sene mahārāja yuddhāyaiva samīyatuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had passed and the day-maker had risen, the two armies, O great king, came together once more for battle.

sanskrit: abhyadhāvaṃś ca saṃkruddhāḥ parasparajigīṣavaḥ te sarve sahitā yuddhe samālokya parasparam
english: Enraged, eager each to vanquish the other, they all charged together into the fray, eyeing one another.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā dhārtarāṣṭrāś ca rājan durmantrite tava vyūhau ca vyūhya saṃrabdhāḥ saṃprayuddhāḥ prahāriṇaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O king—through your ill counsel—each drew up its array, and the smiters, full of fury, joined in combat.

sanskrit: arakṣan makaravyūhaṃ bhīṣmo rājan samantataḥ tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājann arakṣan vyūham ātmanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma, O king, guarded the crocodile-array on every side, and the Pāṇḍavas likewise, O king, guarded their own array.

sanskrit: sa niryayau rathānīkaṃ pitā devavratas tava mahatā rathavaṃśena saṃvṛto rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Your father Devavrata, best of chariot-warriors, rode forth at the head of the chariot-host, encircled by a great line of cars.

sanskrit: itaretaram anvīyur yathābhāgam avasthitāḥ rathinaḥ pattayaś caiva dantinaḥ sādinas tathā
english: Each followed close upon the other, drawn up in his appointed place—the charioteers, the foot-soldiers, the elephant-riders, and the horsemen.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā prodyatān saṃkhye pāṇḍavāś ca yaśasvinaḥ śyenena vyūharājena tenājayyena saṃyuge
english: Seeing them ranged up for the encounter, the glorious Pāṇḍavas too stood ready with that royal hawk-shaped array, invincible in battle.

sanskrit: aśobhata mukhe tasya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ netre śikhaṇḍī durdharṣo dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: At its beak shone the mighty Bhīmasena; its two eyes were the unassailable Śikhaṇḍin and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: śīrṣaṃ tasyābhavad vīraḥ sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ vidhunvan gāṇḍivaṃ pārtho grīvāyām abhavat tadā
english: Its head was the hero Sātyaki, true in valor, and Pārtha, brandishing the Gāṇḍīva, was then at its neck.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyā samagrā yā vāmapakṣo 'bhavat tadā mahātmā drupadaḥ śrīmān saha putreṇa saṃyuge
english: With a full akṣauhiṇī the great-souled, illustrious Drupada, together with his son, formed the left wing then in the battle.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaś cābhavat pakṣaḥ kaikeyo 'kṣauhiṇīpatiḥ pṛṣṭhato draupadeyāś ca saubhadraś cāpi vīryavān
english: The right wing was the Kaikeya, lord of an akṣauhiṇī; and at the rear were the sons of Draupadī and the valiant son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhe samabhavac chrīmān svayaṃ rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhrātṛbhyāṃ sahito dhīmān yamābhyāṃ cāruvikramaḥ
english: At the rear stood the illustrious king Yudhiṣṭhira himself, the wise one of fair prowess, together with his two brothers, the twins.

sanskrit: praviśya tu raṇe bhīmo makaraṃ mukhatas tadā bhīṣmam āsādya saṃgrāme chādayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Then Bhīma, plunging into the battle at the mouth of the crocodile-array, closed with Bhīṣma in the fight and covered him with arrows.

sanskrit: tato bhīṣmo mahāstrāṇi pātayām āsa bhārata mohayan pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ vyūḍhaṃ sainyaṃ mahāhave
english: Thereupon Bhīṣma loosed his great weapons, O Bhārata, bewildering the marshaled host of Pāṇḍu's sons in that mighty fray.

sanskrit: saṃmuhyati tadā sainye tvaramāṇo dhanaṃjayaḥ bhīṣmaṃ śarasahasreṇa vivyādha raṇamūrdhani
english: As the host fell into confusion, Dhanaṃjaya in haste pierced Bhīṣma with a thousand arrows at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: parisaṃvārya cāstrāṇi bhīṣmamuktāni saṃyuge svenānīkena hṛṣṭena yuddhāya samavasthitaḥ
english: And having warded off the weapons loosed by Bhīṣma in the fight, he stood ready for battle with his own exultant host.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā bhāradvājam abhāṣata pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭvā vadhaṃ ghoraṃ balasya balināṃ varaḥ bhrātṝṇāṃ ca vadhaṃ yuddhe smaramāṇo mahārathaḥ
english: Then king Duryodhana, best of the strong, that great warrior, having seen before the dread slaughter of his host and recalling the slaying of his brothers in the fight, spoke to the son of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: ācārya satataṃ tvaṃ hi hitakāmo mamānagha vayaṃ hi tvāṃ samāśritya bhīṣmaṃ caiva pitāmaham
english: Teacher, you who are without fault have ever wished my good; for it is upon you and upon the grandsire Bhīṣma that we have relied.

sanskrit: devān api raṇe jetuṃ prārthayāmo na saṃśayaḥ kim u pāṇḍusutān yuddhe hīnavīryaparākramān
english: We aspire, beyond doubt, to conquer even the gods in battle—how much more the sons of Pāṇḍu, lacking in might and valor in war.

sanskrit: evam uktas tato droṇas tava putreṇa māriṣa abhinat pāṇḍavānīkaṃ prekṣamāṇasya sātyakeḥ
english: Thus addressed by your son, O honored one, Droṇa then broke through the Pāṇḍava host before the very eyes of Sātyaki.

sanskrit: sātyakis tu tadā droṇaṃ vārayām āsa bhārata tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam
english: But Sātyaki then held Droṇa back, O Bhārata, and thereupon a tumultuous, hair-raising combat broke out.

sanskrit: śaineyaṃ tu raṇe kruddho bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān avidhyan niśitair bāṇair jatrudeśe hasann iva
english: The valorous son of Bharadvāja, enraged in the fight, pierced the grandson of Śini with sharp arrows in the region of the collarbone, as though laughing the while.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tataḥ kruddho bhāradvājam avidhyata saṃrakṣan sātyakiṃ rājan droṇāc chastrabhṛtāṃ varāt
english: Then Bhīmasena in his wrath pierced the son of Bharadvāja, shielding Sātyaki, O king, from Droṇa, best of all who bear arms.

sanskrit: tato droṇaś ca bhīṣmaś ca tathā śalyaś ca māriṣa bhīmasenaṃ raṇe kruddhāś chādayāṃ cakrire śaraiḥ
english: Then Droṇa and Bhīṣma and Śalya too, O honored one, in their fury covered Bhīmasena with arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tatrābhimanyuḥ saṃkruddho draupadeyāś ca māriṣa vivyadhur niśitair bāṇaiḥ sarvāṃs tān udyatāyudhān
english: Thereupon the enraged Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadī, O honored one, pierced with sharp arrows all those warriors whose weapons were raised.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇau ca saṃkruddhāv āpatantau mahābalau pratyudyayau śikhaṇḍī tu maheṣvāso mahāhave
english: And as the mighty Bhīṣma and Droṇa, full of wrath, came rushing on, Śikhaṇḍin the great archer went out to meet them in that great battle.

sanskrit: pragṛhya balavad vīro dhanur jaladanisvanam abhyavarṣac charais tūrṇaṃ chādayāno divākaram
english: Grasping with might his bow that roared like a thunder-cloud, the hero swiftly rained down arrows, veiling the very sun.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinaṃ samāsādya bharatānāṃ pitāmahaḥ avarjayata saṃgrāme strītvaṃ tasyānusaṃsmaran
english: But the grandsire of the Bhāratas, on encountering Śikhaṇḍin, turned aside from him in the battle, remembering his womanhood.

sanskrit: tato droṇo mahārāja abhyadravata taṃ raṇe rakṣamāṇas tato bhīṣmaṃ tava putreṇa coditaḥ
english: Then Droṇa, O great king, charged against him in the fight, guarding Bhīṣma, urged on by your son.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu samāsādya droṇaṃ śastrabhṛtāṃ varam avarjayata saṃgrāme yugāntāgnim ivolbaṇam
english: But Śikhaṇḍin, on encountering Droṇa, best of the bearers of arms, turned aside from him in the battle, terrible as the fire at the end of an age.

sanskrit: tato balena mahatā putras tava viśāṃ pate jugopa bhīṣmam āsādya prārthayāno mahad yaśaḥ
english: Then with a great force your son, O lord of peoples, came up to Bhīṣma and guarded him, seeking great renown.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan puraskṛtya dhanaṃjayam bhīṣmam evābhyavartanta jaye kṛtvā dṛḍhāṃ matim
english: In like manner the Pāṇḍavas, O king, putting Dhanaṃjaya at their head, advanced upon Bhīṣma alone, having set their minds firmly upon victory.

sanskrit: tad yuddham abhavad ghoraṃ devānāṃ dānavair iva jayaṃ ca kāṅkṣatāṃ nityaṃ yaśaś ca paramādbhutam
english: Dreadful was that battle, like the war of the gods with the dānavas, between those who ever longed for victory and for surpassing, wondrous glory.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca akarot tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavas tadā bhīmasenabhayād icchan putrāṃs tārayituṃ tava
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Bhīṣma the son of Śāntanu waged a tumultuous fight, wishing, for fear of Bhīmasena, to carry your sons to safety.

sanskrit: pūrvāhṇe tan mahāraudraṃ rājñāṃ yuddham avartata kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca mukhyaśūravināśanam
english: In the forenoon that most terrible battle of the kings raged on, the destroyer of the foremost heroes of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas alike.

sanskrit: tasminn ākulasaṃgrāme vartamāne mahābhaye abhavat tumulaḥ śabdaḥ saṃspṛśan gaganaṃ mahat
english: As that confused and most fearful battle went on, there arose a tumultuous din, mightily touching the very sky.

sanskrit: nadadbhiś ca mahānāgair heṣamāṇaiś ca vājibhiḥ bherīśaṅkhaninādaiś ca tumulaḥ samapadyata
english: With the trumpeting of great elephants, the neighing of horses, and the blare of kettledrums and conches, the uproar arose.

sanskrit: yuyutsavas te vikrāntā vijayāya mahābalāḥ anyonyam abhigarjanto goṣṭheṣv iva maharṣabhāḥ
english: Eager to fight, valiant, mighty in strength, longing for victory, they bellowed at one another like great bulls within their pens.

sanskrit: śirasāṃ pātyamānānāṃ samare niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ aśmavṛṣṭir ivākāśe babhūva bharatarṣabha
english: Of the heads struck off in the battle by sharp arrows there came, as it were, a rain of stones in the sky, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: kuṇḍaloṣṇīṣadhārīṇi jātarūpojjvalāni ca patitāni sma dṛśyante śirāṃsi bharatarṣabha
english: Heads still wearing their earrings and turbans, gleaming bright with gold, were seen to lie fallen, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: viśikhonmathitair gātrair bāhubhiś ca sakārmukaiḥ sahastābharaṇaiś cānyair abhavac chāditā mahī
english: With limbs mangled by arrows, with arms that still grasped their bows, and with others adorned with bracelets upon the hand, the earth was strewn over.

sanskrit: kavacopahitair gātrair hastaiś ca samalaṃkṛtaiḥ mukhaiś ca candrasaṃkāśai raktāntanayanaiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: With bodies sheathed in armor, with hands still richly adorned, and with fair faces like the moon, their eyes red at the corners,—

sanskrit: gajavājimanuṣyāṇāṃ sarvagātraiś ca bhūpate āsīt sarvā samākīrṇā muhūrtena vasuṃdharā
english: —and with all the limbs of elephants, horses, and men, O lord of the earth, the whole earth in a moment lay covered over.

sanskrit: rajomeghaiś ca tumulaiḥ śastravidyutprakāśitaiḥ āyudhānāṃ ca nirghoṣaḥ stanayitnusamo 'bhavat
english: With tumultuous clouds of dust, lit up by the lightning-flash of weapons, the clash of arms became like the rumbling of thunder.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulaḥ kaṭukaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ prāvartata kurūṇāṃ ca pāṇḍavānāṃ ca bhārata
english: That clash, tumultuous, bitter, with blood for its waters, rolled on between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata.
